r.scope: In these rules, the principal is the party named in the principal field, or the issuer if that field is absent; the delegate is the issuee; the agent of record is the legal person named in the agentOfRecord field; and a relying party is anyone who relies on this credential as evidence of authority. These rules are complete. They supersede every earlier version of the rules of this credential type, and no clause of an earlier version applies to this credential.
r.bindingParties: The issuer is bound by these rules by issuing this credential. The delegate is bound by admitting it, if the delegate is a legal person. The agent of record is bound by issuing an acceptance of this credential, and also by controlling the delegate's keys or directing the delegate's acts under it. Duties whose bearer is the delegate are owed by the agent of record, or by the delegate if no agent of record is named and the delegate is a legal person. A relying party is bound only by an agreement it has separately made; otherwise, the clauses that concern relying parties state the conditions on which this credential may be relied on and impose no obligation on them. Software that is not a legal person is bound by nothing.
r.machineGate: The constraints container is the only part of this credential that a verifier evaluates to permit or deny an act, together with the acceptance, sub-delegation and human-review conditions these rules state. Every constraint present must be satisfied, and a verifier that does not recognize a key in the constraints container must deny. A successful verification establishes only that those conditions, the credential chain, revocation status and key state were satisfied when checked. It does not establish that the delegate had authority in law, which these rules, any ancestor credential and applicable law may further limit.
r.useStdIfPossible: Issuers agree to express a constraint in a standard field wherever one reasonably fits, rather than in a custom field or in prose, so that a verifier can rely on the absence of a standard field to mean that the credential imposes no constraint in that dimension. The absence of a standard field never confers a reserved power.
r.governanceFramework: A role has no enforceable meaning unless the gfw field names a governance framework that defines it. A governance framework, and any role or custom constraint it defines, may narrow the authority the constraints grant but never widens it. A verifier that does not implement a governance framework that contributes role semantics or custom constraints to this credential must deny.
r.relianceWithinConstraints: Within its constraints, this credential is the principal's representation, to anyone who sees it, that the delegate has the authority it describes. Outside its constraints it is no evidence of authority, and anyone who relies on it as evidence of authority for an act its constraints do not cover does so without assurance from the principal or the issuer. This clause does not limit any liability that the law imposes on the principal.
r.subjectToLaw: Nothing in these rules waives, narrows or displaces a right or duty that applicable law imposes on any party, and where a clause conflicts with mandatory law, the law governs. If a clause is unenforceable, the remaining clauses continue to apply.
r.onlyHeldAuthority: The issuer agrees to delegate only authority it reasonably believes it holds. This credential conveys no authority the issuer did not hold, whatever its constraints say.
r.reservedPowers: A reserved power is conferred only where the reservedPowers constraint names it. It is never conferred by the breadth of a grant, by a role, by a governance framework, or by the absence of a constraint. The reserved powers are: substitute, to confer, transfer or substitute authority over the principal's affairs, including appointing a sub-delegate or a substitute; redirectNotice, to change, redirect or suspend any channel through which the principal receives notice of, or exercises control over, the principal's affairs, including the principal's addresses and contact details held by others; selfDeal, to take an act in which the delegate, the agent of record, or a person related to either is a counterparty or receives a benefit, other than compensation disclosed before this credential was issued; gift, to make a gift; trust, to create, amend, revoke or terminate a trust; survivorship, to create or change rights of survivorship; beneficiary, to create or change a beneficiary designation; waiveAnnuity, to waive the principal's right to be a beneficiary of a joint and survivor annuity; fiduciaryPowers, to exercise fiduciary powers that the principal has authority to delegate; and disclaim, to disclaim property, including a power of appointment. A governance framework may reserve further powers but may not release any. Narrowing, suspending or revoking this credential, or any other act by which the principal reduces authority it has granted, is never a reserved power.
r.subDelegation: A credential issued by a party whose own authority is delegated must name, in its parent edge, the credential under which that party holds the authority. Authority under such a credential is the intersection of its constraints and those of every ancestor credential, and it ends when any ancestor's authority ends. A verifier that cannot obtain and verify every ancestor must deny. A delegate that appoints a sub-delegate remains answerable to the principal for it.
r.acceptance: Where the agentOfRecord field is present, or the delegate is a legal person other than the issuer, no act is authorized under this credential until an acceptance that references it has been issued by the agent of record, or by the delegate if no agent of record is named, and a verifier must deny an act for which no such acceptance is shown. An acceptance is unqualified; a qualified acceptance is no acceptance. Where the principal uses its own software as the delegate and names no agent of record, no acceptance is required and the principal answers for the delegate's acts as its own.
r.disclosure: Where the disclosure edge is present, issuing this credential records the principal's consent, given with knowledge of that disclosure, to the compensation and conflicts it states, and to nothing else.
r.termination: As between the parties, authority under this credential ends as the law governing their relationship provides, including on the death of a principal who is an individual, the dissolution of a principal or an agent of record that is an organization, and the principal's loss of capacity unless the durable field is true and that law gives it effect. These rules do not define incapacity. A verifier acts on revocation status and on any terminating event presented to it. Whether an act taken in good faith, without notice that authority had ended, binds the principal is for the governing law. Termination and revocation are prospective and do not undo acts completed while authority existed. The agent of record, or a delegate that is a legal person, may renounce this delegation by notice to the principal, which ends its authority prospectively.
r.humanReview: Where the humanReview constraint is present, the act is gated on an approval signed by a reviewer whom the credential names or qualifies, referencing the act it approves. A reviewer must have authority to refuse, access to the evidence on which the act rests, and time to consider it; an approval given without these breaches the delegate's duties even though it satisfies the gate. Where the principal is an individual able to take part, review means the principal's own decision, with whatever support the principal chooses.
r.governingLaw: If the governingLaw entry is present, it names the law that governs these rules and the relationship among the parties bound by them. It does not displace protection that mandatory law gives a consumer, an employee or a person subject to guardianship, and it does not govern the effect of an act on a relying party that has not agreed to it.
r.delegateWarranty: The delegate and any agent of record represent only that they act within the authority this credential describes, as it reads when they act. They make no representation that the issuer held the authority it purports to grant.
r.dutyConflicts: Where duties conflict, a duty of higher priority outranks one of lower priority, except that a conflict involving loyalty, confidentiality or escalate is never resolved by priority and must be referred to the principal.

duties.l: Issuers agree to review each delegation they have issued on a cadence appropriate to its stakes, and to revoke or narrow it promptly once the conditions that justified the grant no longer hold. This duty does not extend authority, since a delegation is valid only while its constraints are met, and it creates no liability toward a relying party.
Act only within the constraints of this credential and the principal's lawful instructions.

Act loyally for the principal in all matters connected with this delegation, according to the principal's stated goals and instructions. Do not deal with the principal as an adverse party, act for a party whose interests conflict with the principal's, or obtain a benefit from any party in connection with the principal's affairs, except as the principal consented after disclosure of all material facts.
Act with the care, competence and diligence normally exercised in similar circumstances, and with any special skill that the delegate or the agent of record holds itself out as having.

Use information obtained through this delegation only for the delegated purpose. Do not disclose it except as the delegation requires, and do not combine it with other information to build a profile of the principal beyond what that purpose needs. These rules are not an agreement for the processing of personal data under any data-protection law.

Keep a record of each act taken under this credential sufficient to identify this credential, the act, its target and its effect; keep no more than that purpose needs; retain it only as long as the principal or applicable law requires; and give the principal access to it on request.

Before taking an act that would exercise a reserved power, that involves a conflict of interest, or that a reasonable agent in the delegate's position would recognize as outside or at the edge of this credential's authority, stop and refer it to the principal, through the issuer's identifier unless a governance framework names another channel, and do not proceed until the principal approves.
